CHIEF COMPLAINT
Annual exam

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Evelyn is a 56-year-old female with past medical history significant for coronary artery disease with prior stenting, prior carpal tunnel release, and herniated disc presenting for annual exam. Patient reports that her herniated disc has been doing well since steroid injection several months ago with no back pain or limitations in movement. Carpal tunnel symptoms have resolved since prior surgical release; patient is back to work with full range of motion and no numbness or tingling. Patient endorses new onset chest pain over the last month that occurs with walking and resolves with rest. Denies chest pain at rest. Describes pain as burning sensation located in the middle of chest, occurring approximately three times per week. States symptoms are not severe enough to warrant emergency evaluation. Denies associated shortness of breath, nausea, or vomiting. Reports nasal congestion from allergies related to pollen.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient endorses chest pain and nasal congestion. Denies shortness of breath, nausea, vomiting, lower extremity edema, muscle aches, or fever/chills.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Coronary artery disease with prior stenting
Prior carpal tunnel release
Herniated disc with prior steroid injection

MEDICATIONS
Aspirin
Toprol

ALLERGIES
Pollen allergies

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is currently working

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Blood pressure well controlled, oxygenation normal
Heart: Slight 3/6 systolic ejection murmur
Lungs: Clear bilaterally
Carotid arteries: No bruits appreciated
Extremities: No lower extremity edema; healed surgical scars on right wrist

RESULTS
Echocardiogram from prior year: Left ventricular ejection fraction 45%, mild mitral regurgitation
EKG: Stable, reflects prior coronary artery disease, no new changes

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Carpal tunnel release: Patient doing well with no recurrent symptoms. No further intervention needed at this time. Patient to notify if symptoms recur.
2. Herniated disc: Patient doing well with good pain control. No further steroid injection or physical therapy needed at this time. Patient to notify if symptoms recur.
3. Coronary artery disease with recurrent chest pain: Continue aspirin and Toprol. Order cardiac stress test to evaluate for additional blockages. Obtain lipid panel. Start Crestor 20 mg once daily. Nurse will assist with scheduling stress test. Follow up as indicated by test results.
